messages:
ops-alert-bot: Heads up — scheduled maintenance for inference fleet in us-west-2 on 2026-03-24.
ops-alert-bot: Window: 2026-03-24 02:00 UTC -> 2026-03-24 05:00 UTC. Reason: GPU driver + kernel security patch. Affects: hosted API and Dedicated pools in us-west-2 (rolling across racks). Private deployments not affected.
ops-alert-bot: Expected customer impact: brief latency spikes (~10-30s) during node reboots; small chance of 502/504 for a tiny percentage of requests if requests hit a node being recycled. No planned downtime, but we want to proactively notify customers and have on-call ready to mitigate.
ops-alert-bot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/infra/patch-gpu-rolling (please ack and attach status page draft)

Maria C: ack, I'll own customer comms. Draft below for email/status page — please review and shorten if we need a lighter message for status page.
Maria C: ```
Customer-facing blurb (status page):
We are performing scheduled maintenance in our us-west-2 inference region on 2026-03-24 between 02:00–05:00 UTC. You may experience short latency increases or transient errors for a small subset of requests. We do not expect sustained outages. If you see persistent issues, please contact support.

Customer email draft:
Subject: Scheduled maintenance in US-West on 24 March — minor, short-lived impact possible
Body: Hello,
We will be performing maintenance on our inference fleet in US-West on 2026-03-24 02:00–05:00 UTC to apply a security update. During the work we may see short latency spikes and very brief errors (<1–2 minutes) for a subset of requests. No action required from you; we will post updates to status.redwood.com. Reach out to support@redwood.com if you see anything impactful.
Thank you,
Redwood Inference Operations
```

Samir P: ack from eng-sre oncall. I'll coordinate the rolling reboots. Plan:
- stagger by rack, 1 node at a time per shard
- pre-warm KV caches on target nodes before draining
- set temporary routing weight to reduce traffic to pool-usw2-dedicated-3 until fully reprovisioned
- page escalation: if sustained 5m error rate >5% or P50 latency >2x baseline, call SRE pager

Samir P: Quick ops commands I'll run during window:
```
# drain node
kubectl cordon node/node-045
kubectl drain node/node-045 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# post-patch health-check
curl -sS https://127.0.0.1:9000/health | jq .
```

Jin Park: ack — I'll run canary on 2 nodes first and monitor RL/latency. If we see tail latency > 1s for two consecutive 5m windows, we have pre-approved fallback:
- route traffic to quantized-variant of the model (model-q4a) in same region
- if fallback drops quality below threshold, we'll throttle to 50% and notify Product/Support

Ava (Support): Copy — prepping support playbook and canned replies. Draft internal triage steps below for CS agents — please edit.
Ava (Support): ```
Internal quick triage (support):
1) Check status.redwood.com, note region us-west-2 maintenance window.
2) Ask customer: are you seeing continuous failures, or short spikes?
3) If continuous >5min or significant impact -> open ticket with #incidents, tag @eng-sre oncall and @maria_c
4) Provide this canned reply: "We're performing scheduled maintenance; we're investigating and will update within 15 minutes. Apologies for the inconvenience."
```

Theo (Eng-SRE): Quick Q — can we shift to 02:00–06:00 UTC instead? Historically 04:00 UTC shows slightly higher background jobs. Longer window gives more breathing room for staggered reboots.

ops-alert-bot: Proposal accepted: window updated to 02:00–06:00 UTC. Please confirm final ack if you can adhere to new timing.

Maria C: ack, updated drafts to 02:00–06:00 UTC and shortened status blurb. Preparing to post to status once Samir confirms final start time.

Nadia (Product): One note on SLA language — if any customer experiences service interruption >60s that meets our SLA outage definition, coordinate with finance/sales for credit. Add that to the postmortem checklist please.

Samir P: Understood. I'll add SLA check to postmortem template. Also schedule a quick IR call if we hit the escalation thresholds.

Samir P: Planning note: During the window I'll enable extra metric retention for the region (10s scrape) and open a short-lived grafana dashboard with these panels: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5m error rate, inflight requests, queue length.

Samir P: command snippets I'll use to temporarily change routing weights (ops playbook):
```
# reduce traffic to pool
redwoodctl routing set-weight --pool pool-usw2-dedicated-3 --weight 0.2
# restore
redwoodctl routing set-weight --pool pool-usw2-dedicated-3 --weight 1.0
```

Ava (Support): I'll stage the customer email to go out ~1 hour before start, and a follow-up on completion. Will coordinate with Maria on language.

ops-alert-bot: Reminder: escalation policy — page eng-sre-oncall if error rate >5% for 5m OR if >3% customer-facing 5xxs for 10m. Also page product lead if customer-visible regression in quality is detected.

Samir P: Starting timeline: prechecks at 01:30 UTC (baseline metrics + backups), start rolling reboots at 02:00 UTC. Estimated finish by 06:00 UTC with rollbacks possible if needed.

ops-alert-bot: UPDATE 2026-03-24 06:12 UTC: maintenance completed. All patched nodes report green health. No sustained customer-impacting incidents reported. Closing thread.

Maria C: Posted status update: "Maintenance complete — all systems operational. If you continue to see any issues, please contact support." Posted on status.redwood.com and sent customer follow-up email.

Ava (Support): Support blurb posted to internal triage doc. No major tickets opened during window; two brief spikes closed by auto-retries.

Samir P: Postmortem notes: quantized fallback triggered for 8 minutes for a tiny subset of routes; reverted once tail latency normalized. Captured logs and will file detailed postmortem doc in /incident/1768504321-patch-run.

Theo (Eng-SRE): Thx team — nice coordination. Closing.

ops-alert-bot: Thread closed by ops-alert-bot."
